name: Werewolf
anatomy: Digitigrade canine hindlimbs; four main weight-bearing paw digits; forelimb dewclaw is medial.
appearance: A moderately long canine muzzle, pointed ears, round pupils, dense guard hair and a four-toed paw silhouette.

name: Werecheetah
anatomy: Lean digitigrade limbs; four main paw toes; small, less fully retractile claws.
appearance: A slim short feline muzzle, solid black spots, black tear tracks, rounded ears and round pupils. Keep the body light and the tail long.

name: Werebear
anatomy: Plantigrade hindfeet; five toes with non-retractile claws.
appearance: A broad bear muzzle, rounded ears, heavy shoulder mass and dense coarse fur. Keep the heel on the ground during a planted stance.

name: Werepanther
anatomy: Specify black leopard or black jaguar; digitigrade felid limbs, retractile claws.
appearance: A black leopard hybrid with a broad feline muzzle, rounded ears, round pupils, long tail and faint rosettes visible in reflected light.

name: Werelioness
anatomy: Digitigrade felid limbs; four hind toes, medial forelimb dewclaw; no mane.
appearance: A tawny lioness muzzle, broad nose, rounded ears, round pupils, four main paw toes and a tufted tail.

name: Weretiger
anatomy: Digitigrade felid limbs; retractile claws; round pupils.
appearance: A broad tiger muzzle, rounded ears and orange coat with black stripes that follow the growing anatomy.

name: Werehyena
anatomy: Digitigrade; spotted-hyena variant has four toes per foot.
appearance: A deep muzzle, rounded ears, heavy neck, spotted coarse coat and a sloping shoulder-to-hip silhouette.

name: Werefox
anatomy: Digitigrade canine plan; main paws have four forward digits.
appearance: A narrow orange fox muzzle, large pointed ears, dark lower legs and a full brush tail.

name: Wereboar
anatomy: Even-toed ungulate; two main hooves and smaller side digits.
appearance: A broad mobile snout disc, coarse bristles, compact triangular ears and paired curved tusks.

name: Werebull
anatomy: Cloven hooves; two principal digits and rear dewclaws; paired keratin horns.
appearance: A heavy bovine muzzle, lateral ears, massive neck and a matched pair of unbranched horns growing from the frontal bone.

name: Weredeer
anatomy: Cloven hooves; antlers differ from permanent keratin horns.
appearance: A slender cervid muzzle, broad mobile ears, a soft coat and a paired antler rack if the selected deer phenotype has antlers.

name: Wererat
anatomy: Five hind toes; smaller four main front digits plus reduced thumb.
appearance: A narrow rodent muzzle, rounded bare ears, long whiskers, prominent incisors and a thin scaled tail.

name: Werecrocodile
anatomy: Reptilian limbs; five fore digits and four hind digits for the crocodile endpoint.
appearance: A broad crocodilian muzzle, nostrils near its tip, scaly skin and a muscular laterally flattened tail.

name: Werebat
anatomy: Choose an arm-to-wing conversion; elongate fingers II-V; leave the thumb free.
appearance: A short bat muzzle, large species-appropriate ears and membranes tensioned between elongated fingers. A bat is a mammal, with fur rather than feathers.

name: Wereeagle
anatomy: Avian wing replaces the arm; raptor hindfeet have three forward toes and a rear hallux.
appearance: A hooked eagle beak, layered flight feathers and a predatory avian head; wings attach at the existing shoulders.

name: Wereshark
anatomy: Choose a fantasy hybrid topology explicitly; fins are not jointed mammal paws.
appearance: Smooth grey shark skin, paired side gill slits, a broad shark head and ordered rows of triangular teeth.

name: Werehorse
anatomy: Unguligrade; one principal hoof per limb, no cloven split or bovine dewclaws.
appearance: An equine muzzle, upright mobile ears, a mane, single hooves and a long hair-covered tail.

name: Werecow
anatomy: Bovine cloven hoof anatomy; horned or hornless depends on the selected phenotype.
appearance: A broad moist bovine nose, lateral ears and a black-and-white short coat; use the chosen hornless individual consistently.

name: Bull horns / minotaur
anatomy: A paired, unbranched horn set; no deer-like branching.
appearance: A heavy bovine face and neck, with horns growing sideways from behind the eye line before curving upward.

name: Domestic werecat
anatomy: Digitigrade cat legs; retractile claws; four hind toes and a medial forelimb dewclaw.
appearance: A short domestic-cat muzzle, upright triangular ears, tabby markings and pupils that narrow vertically under brighter light.

name: Wereraven
anatomy: Avian arm-to-wing plan; one head; no mammal ear pinnae at endpoint.
appearance: A straight black raven beak, black contour feathers, layered wing feathers and small round dark eyes.

name: Wereowl
anatomy: Avian arm-to-wing plan; zygodactyl grip can be chosen for perched feet.
appearance: A short hooked beak, a feather facial disc and large forward-facing eyes; rotate the head within plausible limits.

name: Wereram
anatomy: Cloven hooves; paired ridged spiral horns; wool rather than a fur mane.
appearance: A sheep muzzle, dense wool and a matched pair of curling ridged horns that remain clear of the ears.

name: Weregoat
anatomy: Cloven hooves; paired backward-curving horns; horizontal pupils.
appearance: A narrow caprine muzzle, short beard, horizontal pupils and tapered horns sweeping backward.
